A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 26-page versions of the same RoboMD paper, including Appendices A–G. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons establish that substantive content matches throughout.

before.justification: v3 reports original simulation and physical-robot evaluations in Section 4, including failure-diagnosis results and policy fine-tuning outcomes. Appendices B, F, and G contain additional empirical analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results, including UR5e failure rankings in Table 3, embedding evaluations, and fine-tuning results in Tables 5 and 13.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same ViT/CLIP embedding, BCE and contrastive objectives, PPO search, reward function, vulnerability querying, and policy-improvement procedure.

E1.justification: The same simulated manipulation tasks, RoboMimic/MimicGen data, UR5e/SO101 evaluations, and seen/unseen object, lighting, color, and size perturbations appear in both versions, including the appendices.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same A2C, SAC, VLM, CNN, and ResNet comparators, including GPT-4o with five-shot demonstrations. The fine-tuning comparison strategies in Tables 5 and 13 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The 500 success-failure pairs, ranking and accuracy evaluations, perturbation procedures, model configurations, and training settings are identical in Section 4 and Appendices B–D, F, and G.

E4.justification: Both retain identical loss and modality ablations, embedding grouping and semantic-continuity tests, kNN analysis, robustness examples, and fine-tuning analyses in the main text and appendices.

E5.justification: Statistical and uncertainty reporting is identical throughout. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval, significance-testing, or uncertainty-estimation information is added, removed, or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results, rankings, and plotted findings match. For example, Tables 5 and 13 retain accuracies of 67.91% before fine-tuning, 92.83% with RoboMD-guided fine-tuning, and 85.48% with all-failure fine-tuning.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations in Section 3, its three theorems, and Appendix A's assumptions, lemmas, derivations, and proofs are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about semantic-space vulnerability diagnosis, generalization to unseen variations, comparative performance, and data-efficient policy improvement.

C2.justification: Interpretations of embedding continuity, failure versus OOD detection, multimodal learning, and fine-tuning tradeoffs are unchanged. The stated applicability boundaries and future-work discussion also match.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement, code link, hardware/software specifications, encoder details, baseline hyperparameters, and action-description mapping remain unchanged in Section 7 and Appendices B–F.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, reference list, and positioning relative to OOD detection, supervised failure prediction, and active failure search are identical.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025' to 'ICLR 2026'. The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v3, 16 Mar 2026, to v4, 18 May 2026. Body wording, terminology, and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions, axes, legends, placement, and page layout are unchanged. Rendered-page differences are confined to the header year and first-page arXiv stamp, which are text updates covered under P1.

improvement.justification: v4 updates publication and version metadata while preserving all substantive text, experiments, results, proofs, reproducibility details, and displays, including the appendices. These updates establish no meaningful net difference in scientific quality or readability.
